fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the street in both directions.
• Keep at least one parking area clear of vehicles to give responders room to stage equipment.
• Mark or label all access points on the exterior so responders can quickly identify which entry leads to which part of the property.
• Post the location of the solar panel system's emergency shutoff in a visible location near the main electrical panel or primary entry door.
• Notify your local fire department of the solar panel installation so responders are aware before arriving on scene.
• Keep walkways clear of potted plants, stored items, or landscaping that narrows the path for responders carrying equipment.
• Trim any landscaping that obstructs sightlines to access points from the street or parking area.
• If the driveway does not allow vehicles to turn around, install a turnaround area or keep a clear pull-forward space so responders do not have to back out under emergency conditions.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin scattered trees near structures to increase open space between tree canopies and rooflines.
• Separate any tree clusters that are close enough to allow fire to move directly from one tree to another toward the house.
• Trim lower branches on scattered trees to raise the canopy height above shrub level.
• Remove shrubs growing directly beneath tree canopies near structures.
• Keep shrubs scattered across the property trimmed low and spaced apart so fire cannot easily move between them.
• Maintain the existing open areas around structures by keeping new vegetation from filling in over time.
